predecessors.name: Malwa culture
predecessors.text: Daimabad and Inamgaon, sites of both cultures; 'The Jorwe culture was preceded by the Malwa culture'

ledger.x: c. 1400 BCE: the Jorwe culture appears in the Maharashtra Deccan. 'The early phase of the culture is dated to c. 1400-1000 BCE'; 'existed in large areas of the Deccan region in what is now Maharashtra state'. The year is the page's; the country is my reading of the named sites.

c. 1400 BCE: Daimabad and Inamgaon pass from the Malwa culture to the Jorwe. Both pages list the two sites; 'The Jorwe culture was preceded by the Malwa culture'; the Malwa page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa_culture) has it 'succeeded by the Jorwe culture'.

c. 1300 BCE: the Jorwe culture reaches the Malwa plateau. The page says the culture 'also reached north into the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh' and lists Navdatoli near Maheshwar; the Malwa page ends 'c. 1300 BCE' ('mainly dated to c. 1600 - c. 1300 BCE'). No page dates the northward spread; -1300 is the end of the…

c. 700 BCE: the last Jorwe settlements are abandoned. 'Most Jorwe culture sites were abandoned around 1000 BCE... after which the remaining sites show growing poverty until their abandonment around 700 BCE'; succeeded by 'the Iron Age megalithic culture of the Deccan and the Northern Black Polished Ware culture'…

certainty.note: An archaeological culture known from about 200 settlements; the page names no rivers or districts and the land abandoned around 1000 BCE is not placed.
